html:
An Akan kingdom at the northern edge of the forest in central Ghana, centred on Bono Manso near Techiman, which grew from about the 13th or 14th century and is often called the cradle of the Akan states.

It traded gold and kola nuts north through the market town of Begho to Mande merchants, who carried them to Djenne and the Mali Empire. Many Akan customs of kingship, gold weights and the use of stools as symbols of office are traced to Bono. In 1723 the expanding Asante kingdom conquered it. See also Akan goldweights and the Akan peoples.
